title: Safely deploy and automate ML and AI workflows
objective: Select inference methods, resources, pipelines, approvals, and rollback procedures according to requirements, and operate them reproducibly.

prerequisites.title: Prepare Data for ML and AI
Evaluate ML Models and Foundation Models Against Requirements

sections.title: Choose an inference mode based on the request pattern
paragraphs: Deployment engineers compare real-time, asynchronous, and batch inference modes based on response time, throughput, input size, how results are returned to users, and cost. Online requests that require consistently low latency and forecasts that can be processed in large volumes overnight require different endpoints and scaling strategies.

Amazon SageMaker AI is a fully managed service that lets you build and train models, then deploy them to hosting environments ready for operation. Even after deploying a model, you compare the input format, authentication, network reachability, timeout, error responses, and capacity against user requirements.

The diagram compares where predictions are run and how results are delivered. With real-time inference, the endpoint responds immediately. With asynchronous inference, requests to the endpoint are placed in a queue, and the processing results are stored in Amazon S3. When the input files are already available in Amazon S3 and the results can be collected later in batches, you can run a Batch Transform job without setting up an endpoint.

sources.label: MLA-C02 Exam Guide: Deployment and Orchestration

sections.title: Putting Quality Gates in the Pipeline
paragraphs: An ML pipeline is not simply a sequence connecting data preparation, training, evaluation, registration, and deployment. It explicitly defines the inputs and outputs of each stage, success criteria, what stops when a failure occurs, the execution role, and the approver, preventing models that fail evaluation from moving into production.

When using a model registry and an approval workflow, associate the model artifacts, evaluation results, data and code versions, and the basis for approval. Being able to use the same inputs when rerunning a pipeline and track which version was deployed to which environment are prerequisites for rollback.

sections.title: Limit User Impact with Progressive Delivery
paragraphs: When releasing a new model, identify the traffic directed to the existing and candidate models, then compare quality, latency, error rate, cost, and safety within a limited scope. A/B testing and progressive delivery become merely simultaneous operation unless the comparison targets and success criteria are defined in advance.

Record the deployment version, configuration, endpoint assignments, and rollback decision-maker so that you can immediately return to a known-good model if an anomaly occurs. Even if the candidate model performs better, do not expand its rollout unless it meets the safety and service objectives.

sources.label: MLA-C02 Exam Guide: Workflow Deployment and Orchestration

checkpoints.prompt: An operations staff member in the accounting department needs to process several million invoices in a single inference job every night and receive the results from Amazon S3 by the following morning. Immediate responses to users are not required, and operational constraints prevent creating an inference endpoint. Which inference method meets these requirements?

choices.text: Use SageMaker Batch Transform to process the invoice data in S3 in a single job and save the results to S3.
choices.explanation: Batch Transform processes S3 input as a job and writes the results to S3 without creating an inference endpoint.

choices.text: Use SageMaker asynchronous inference to queue invoice-processing requests overnight and save the results to S3.
choices.explanation: Asynchronous inference can write results to S3, but it requires creating an inference endpoint to receive the requests.

choices.text: Prepare a SageMaker real-time inference endpoint, send the invoices one at a time, and receive the results.
choices.explanation: Real-time inference requires an endpoint. It also does not fit these requirements because immediate responses are unnecessary and the results need to be received in a batch by the following morning.

checkpoints.prompt: The owner of a model-update pipeline wants to prevent models that fail evaluation from reaching production. Which design is most appropriate?

choices.text: Automatically overwrite the production model with every model that completes training.
choices.explanation: There is no boundary between evaluation and approval.

choices.text: Do not record model versions or provide rollback when failures occur.
choices.explanation: There is no way to return to a known good state during an incident.

choices.text: Use the evaluation success criteria as a quality gate, and allow registration and deployment only after recording the evaluation results, model version, and rationale for approval.
choices.explanation: Models that fail to meet the criteria are stopped, and the reason for adoption can be traced.

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for gradually deploying a candidate model must decide whether to expand the rollout. Which is the most appropriate decision-making method?

choices.text: Identify the candidate and existing models, and compare quality, latency, error rate, cost, and safety with limited traffic. If the cost or safety threshold is exceeded, do not expand the rollout even if quality is better.
choices.explanation: This limits the impact on users and allows the rollout to be expanded only when all criteria, including the changed conditions, are met.

choices.text: If the candidate model has higher accuracy, switch all traffic without checking the cost or safety thresholds.
choices.explanation: This would deploy the model even if production requirements other than quality exceed their thresholds, overlooking the changed conditions.

choices.text: Stop monitoring after deployment without deciding where to roll back in the event of an issue.
choices.explanation: Problems cannot be detected or recovered from.
